headline: I Am The Sole Global Courier Tasked With Personally Rowing A Paper Boat Through The Strait Of Hormuz
body:
As the world’s only maritime mediator equipped with nothing but a packet of glue and some spare printer paper, I really felt the pressure today when I was told my seven-day navigation plan had been rejected. I spent the last three weeks folding a pristine A4 sheet into a sturdy frigate, only for a high-ranking official to look me in the eye and say it lacked the structural integrity required for international diplomacy.

I honestly thought the plan was foolproof. I had charted a course that hugged the coastline precisely, avoiding all major tankers while ensuring I arrived at the international shipping lane exactly by Thursday. I even practiced my 'peaceful wave' technique for five hours in my bathtub. It's truly disheartening to see such meticulous hand-crafted logistics dismissed simply because the vessel doesn't have a built-in radar system.

Now I’m stuck here on the shore with a soggy origami hull, trying to convince the local authorities that a paper boat is technically a 'stealth vessel' because it’s invisible to modern military sonar. If I don't get the go-ahead soon, the entire regional stability of my afternoon will be ruined. I just wanted to be the one to bridge the gap, but apparently, world powers prefer steel to stationery.
caption: When the high seas meet office supplies, diplomacy takes a dive. Should I upgrade to cardstock or just give up on my maritime dreams? 🚢📝 #Diplomacy #Origami #StraitOfHormuz #Geopolitics (satire)
igHook: Would you trust a diplomat who uses glue sticks instead of treaties?
